The story does not have a balance between the two elements; instead, it relies exclusively on "scene." Written in the format of a dramatic script, the entire narrative unfolds in real-time through dialogue and brief physical actions (stage directions). There is no narrative summary to compress time, nor is there direct exposition to explain the characters' shared history—everything about their past and relationship must be inferred by the reader from their real-time interaction.
